messages.subject: Variable number of ongoing tasks
parts:
Hello,

I have a problem where the number of transactions changes and I cannot figure out how best to implement it in simmer.

Let's say there are a lot of tasks waiting to be implemented, each taking an integer number of days (with a Poisson distribution).

There are, say, 10 people available.

A task may require more than one person (most require a single person).

I want to keep all people busy every day.  The number of tasks on any given day is likely to vary.

An example case: on a given day there may be 6 people already committed to tasks.  The remaining 4 people may start between 1 task (requiring 4 people), 4 tasks (each requiring one person) or some combination.

The task duration and number of people required are chosen at random (this is not true in reality, but I am trying to keep things simple).

I have created scripts with:

add_resource("person", capacity=10)

and with

add_resource("person_1", capacity=1)
add_resource("person_2", capacity=1)
etc

and a queue for cases where insufficient people are available for the task

But I can never keep everybody occupied.

I am trying to keep user written functions to a minimum, i.e., rely on simmer functions and options.  But this approach does not appear possible.

Suggestions welcome.

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Variable number of ongoing tasks
parts:
Hi, 

If people are chosen at random, you can use a single resource with capacity=10. Otherwise, you need to split it in individual resources, and then use select() with the policy that better suits your problem (or define your own). If you cannot keep everybody occupied, it means that there are not enough tasks. I see no other reason for this.

Regards,
Iñaki

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Variable number of ongoing tasks
parts:
Iñaki,

Thanks for the prompt reply.

There was a bug in my code caused by a misunderstanding on my part.  I thought the trajectory name was more of a comment.  In the Introduction to simmer Vignette, the code:

patient <- trajectory("patients' path") %>%

has patient with and without an s, but always uses it without an s

add_generator("patient", patient, function() rnorm(1, 10, 2))

Changing the code below to use add_generator("feature", feature, at(rep(0, 1e2))) produces very different behavior.

Anyway major problem solved :-)
It takes a couple of time steps for the queue to fill, but this is not a problem.

Is there a way to create an infinite queue of pending tasks without flooding the pipeline at the start?

library(gamlss.tr)
library("simmer")

# Create a zero truncated Poisson distribution
gen.trun(family=PO)

env=simmer("impl_env")

feature=trajectory("feature imp") %>%
    set_attribute("num_dev", function() rPOtr(1, 2)) %>%
    seize("developer", function(attrs) attrs[["num_dev"]]) %>%
    timeout(function() rPOtr(1, 2)) %>%
    release("developer", function(attrs) attrs[["num_dev"]])

env %>%
    add_resource("developer", 10) %>%
    add_generator("feature imp", feature, at(rep(0, 1e2)))

env %>%
    run(until=20)

env %>%
    get_mon_arrivals

env %>%
    get_mon_resources
